claims.text: Machine learning-guided compositional optimization can tune magnetic exchange interactions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Machine learning-guided compositional optimization can improve the magnetocaloric effect of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys in low-dimensional settings.
The initial non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys are disordered solid solutions.
A data-driven or machine-learning model can systematically adjust alloy compositions away from fixed equiatomic ratios.
The relevant behavior is measured under applied magnetic fields near the magnetic phase-transition temperature in a constrained low-dimensional geometry.
Local atomic-scale chemical disorder and the distribution of magnetic species modulate magnetic exchange interactions.
Machine-learning optimization can identify compositions that tune local magnetic environments.
Tuning local magnetic environments modifies magnetic exchange couplings.
Modified magnetic exchange couplings shift the magnetic transition temperature.
Shifting the magnetic transition temperature enhances the magnetocaloric response.
Optimized alloys will have a larger magnetic entropy change than conventionally selected non-equiatomic alloys.
Optimized alloys will provide more precise control of magnetic ordering transitions than conventionally selected non-equiatomic alloys.
Intrinsic disorder and low-dimensional effects may constrain the proposed improvement.
